statuses.closed-with-power: Closed with shown power: the search recovers planted texts of this kind, and the cells score like shuffled cells.
statuses.excluded-by-count: Excluded by a count: a statistic no key can change rules it out for ordinary English, without a search.
statuses.tested-without-power: Tested without shown power: nothing was found, but no planted text was recovered, so nothing is closed.
statuses.open: Open: not searched with shown power, or the search cannot yet find planted texts.

families.family: A keyed Polybius square alone (one-to-one letter key)
families.evidence: Planted texts come back; the cells score -3.82 to -3.97 a letter against about -2 for English, also read backwards.

families.family: Columnar and periodic transposition, every order at widths 2 to 9 (and width 10 done), any language
families.evidence: A key-invariant score; planted English and German beat their shuffles by more than the cells in all 24 cases.

families.family: Complete 14-column transposition with a letter key
families.evidence: 18 of 18 planted texts recovered, both directions; the cells score -3.25 to -3.64 a letter, inside their shuffles.

families.family: Double transposition, every pair of orders at widths 2 to 6
families.evidence: In 50 of 50 cases the cells beat their shuffles by less than planted English and German.

families.family: Keyword transpositions (379,521 keywords, single, double and square)
families.evidence: Planted keywords surface near English; the cells' best is under shuffled cells.

families.family: Four-square and two-square
families.evidence: Excluded by a side count (0 of 7,400 keyed English draws reach the cells) and searched: 4 of 6 planted texts recovered, the cells inside their shuffles.

families.family: Nulls by place (every 3rd, 4th, 5th cell, or one grid column)
families.evidence: 6 of 6 planted texts recovered; the cells' best is -3.28 a letter against -2.14 or better for English.

families.family: Homophonic key (several symbols for one letter)
families.evidence: 6 of 6 planted homophonic texts recovered; the cells and the regrouping sit inside their shuffles.

families.family: Any transposition of ordinary English prose under a one-to-one letter key
families.evidence: A transposition keeps letter counts; none of 479,051 prose windows has the cells' flatness, few letters and rare column together.

families.family: Playfair
families.evidence: 10 of 98 pairs repeat a cell, which Playfair never does.

families.family: A fixed code giving each letter one pair of cells
families.evidence: Such a code has at most 25 different pairs; the cells have 79 and 80.

families.family: The five rare symbols as word spaces
families.evidence: Words would average 20.89 letters; held-out English never exceeds 8.5.

families.family: Only the column digit carries the message
families.evidence: The paired column digits are less coincident than any of 373 English windows.

families.family: Eight published readings
families.evidence: None passes as a full-length reading against the counts the cells force; three fail their own stated method.

families.family: A repeating shift on the square (Vigenere-like), periods 2 to 4
families.evidence: Searched under the old 8,689-letter model on the book's letter order; nothing found, no planted text.

families.family: Delays and routes of the row and column digits
families.evidence: Delay 79 reached 3 of 200 shuffles under the old model; no planted text.

families.family: Bifid
families.evidence: All periods 1 to 196; 1,109 of 2,000 shuffles reach the cells' best; no planted text.

families.family: Autokey on the square
families.evidence: 37 of 40 shuffles score as well; no planted text.

families.family: Running key from texts in the repository, and the book's exercise as a key
families.evidence: 94,860 alignments and the exercise slid across the cells; shuffles do as well; no planted text.

families.family: Caesar, Vigenere, Beaufort, Porta and affine on the cells as letters
families.evidence: Under the old model; shuffles score as well; no planted text.

families.family: A plaintext in another language (French, German, Latin, Russian transliteration)
families.evidence: Letter counts only: French 2 of 2,000 and Italian 6 of 2,000 draws as flat. The key-invariant transposition searches cover any language; the substitution searches are English only.
families.next: Fit quadgram models for French, German, Latin and a Russian transliteration, and rerun the keyed-square, nulls and four-square searches with planted texts in each language.

families.family: 14 by 14 turning grille with a letter key
families.evidence: The compiled search finds 4 of 4 planted grilles with the key given and 0 of 4 with it unknown.
families.next: A joint method that recovers planted grilles with the key unknown, before the cells are searched.

families.family: Enciphering errors by the author
families.evidence: Four count moves are needed before the counts look English; the width-14 search tolerates 8 wrong cells.
families.next: Plant texts with random cell errors and measure how many errors each closed search still tolerates.

families.family: No message (a hand construction)
families.evidence: Van Eykelen's tally-and-deal recipe matches all 14 fingerprint statistics; statistics alone cannot decide.
families.next: A predeclared likelihood test between van Eykelen's tally-and-deal recipe and message-bearing models, calibrated on planted texts.

families.family: A general pair table (2 by 2 Hill, any 625-pair code)
families.evidence: The cells' different-pair count is ordinary for prose, so the count does not exclude it.
families.next: Search 2 by 2 Hill over a keyed square with planted texts.

families.family: Transposition beyond the searched widths, or with nulls and an incomplete rectangle
families.evidence: The key-invariant method has no power past width 10; double transposition is closed only to width 6.
families.next: A joint search with a letter key, as for width 14, at widths 11 to 13 and for double transposition above width 6.
